newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian oils firm Trituraf shares oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian oils firm Trituraf shares oversubscribed.

text.p: Shares in oilseed and oils producer Trituraf offered to the public by Ivory Coast were oversubscribed by 107.5 percent, the Abidjan bourse said on Thursday.
The state sold its 10 percent stake, represented by 104,000 shares sold at 6,250 CFA francs apiece, to raise 650 million CFA francs ($1.1 million).
The sale opened on June 2 and was scheduled to last until June 30, but the shares were sold out within four days, the bourse said.
Individuals and institutions put in offers for a total 215,768 shares.

The authorities decided to scale these down in such a way that all the shares went to individuals. The bourse said 82 percent of the stock thus went to small shareholders, with no more than 100 shares each.

Trituraf is majority-owned by Anglo-Dutch food and household products group Unilever, which will retain its 73 percent stake. France's Compagnie Francaise de Developpment des Textiles (CFDT) holds 14 percent and private Ivorian interests have the balance.
The shares were officially introduced onto the bourse on Thursday at the offer price of 6,250 CFA francs. They will begin trading at the next bourse session on Tuesday, August 5. ($ = 618 CFA francs)
